title: Solving for an Unknown Inner Function in a Cubic Composition
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Let f(x) = 2x^3 - 4. Find a function y = g(x) so that the composition satisfies (f o g)(x) = x + 2.

steps.title: Set Up the Composition Equation f(g(x)) = x + 2
steps.explanation: Substitute g(x) into f(x) = 2x^3 - 4 and set the expression equal to the required target x + 2.
steps.why: By definition of composition, (f o g)(x) = 2(g(x))^3 - 4.

steps.title: Isolate the Cubed Term (g(x))^3
steps.explanation: Add 4 to both sides to get x + 6, then divide both sides by 2.
steps.why: Standard inverse arithmetic operations isolate the cube of g(x).

steps.title: Extract the Real Cube Root
steps.explanation: Take the unique real cube root of both sides to obtain g(x) = ((x + 6)/2)^(1/3).
steps.why: The cube function u -> u^3 is strictly increasing and bijective on R, so taking the real cube root uniquely determines g(x).
